RawMaterial.title: RawMaterial
RawMaterial.description: Represents a raw material used in the steel foundry, including its stock level and minimum stock threshold.

id.description: Unique identifier for the raw material.

name.description: Name of the raw material (e.g., ChatarraAcero, ArenaMoldeo).

stock.description: Current stock level of the raw material.

unit.description: Unit of measurement for the raw material (e.g., ton, kg, m3).

min_stock.description: Minimum stock level that should be maintained for the raw material.

Client.title: Client
Client.description: Represents a client of the steel foundry.

ProductionOrder.title: ProductionOrder
ProductionOrder.description: Represents a production order (colada) in the steel foundry.

id.description: Unique identifier for the production order.

status.description: Current status of the production order (e.g., Pendiente, En Proceso, Terminada).

product.description: Product being manufactured in the production order.

qty.description: Quantity of the product to be manufactured.

mp_target_id.description: Reference to RawMaterial. (Relationship: RawMaterial 1:N ProductionOrder). Identifier of the raw material targeted for consumption.

mp_consumption.description: Amount of raw material consumed in the production order.

targetWeek.description: Target week for the production order (ISO week number).

client_id.description: Reference to Client. (Relationship: Client 1:N ProductionOrder). Identifier of the client associated with the production order.

priority.description: Priority of the production order (e.g., Baja, Media, Alta).

job_type.description: Type of job for the production order (e.g., Normal Production, Express/Small Job).

start_time_est.description: Estimated start time of the production order (timestamp).

end_time_est.description: Estimated end time of the production order (timestamp).

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the production order was created.

start_time_real.description: Actual start time of the production order (timestamp).

end_time_real.description: Actual end time of the production order (timestamp).

Incident.title: Incident
Incident.description: Represents an incident or exception that occurred during production.

type.description: Type of incident (e.g., Falla Equipo, Error Humano).

op_id.description: Reference to ProductionOrder. (Relationship: ProductionOrder 1:N Incident). Identifier of the production order associated with the incident (optional).

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore structure is designed to manage raw materials, clients, production orders, and incidents for a steel foundry. The structure emphasizes authorization independence, clarity, and security.  Each user owns their set of data within an `artifacts/{appId}/users/{userId}` path, ensuring data segregation. 

**Authorization Independence:**

*   Authorization is managed through path-based ownership (`/users/{userId}`). Each user has their own collections for materials, clients, production orders, and incidents. This eliminates the need for `get()` calls in security rules to validate ownership, which supports atomic operations and simplifies debugging.

**Structural Segregation:**

*   All documents within a collection share the same security requirements. For example, all production orders in `/artifacts/{appId}/users/{userId}/production_orders` are owned by the user identified by `{userId}`.

**QAPs (Rules are not Filters):**

*   List operations are secured using path-based rules. Since each user's data is stored under their own `userId`, rules can easily enforce that a user can only list documents within their own path.

**Data Clarity and Predictability:**

*   Explicit state modeling is used with the `status` field in the `ProductionOrder` entity, ensuring a clear and easily understandable state for each order.

**Denormalization:**

*   There's no explicit denormalization mentioned because the structure is already designed to avoid hierarchical dependencies. If there were subcollections to `ProductionOrder` that required access control based on the `ProductionOrder`'s data, the relevant fields would be denormalized into those subcollection documents.
